findings.title: Rejected devices are cached before the device-limit decision succeeds
findings.body: `tagDeviceUI` inserts the device ID into the local cache before `CreateOrUpdateDevice` checks/enforces the limit. For a new device at capacity, the first authentication attempt correctly receives `ErrDeviceLimitReached`, but the cache entry remains. A subsequent request from the same device ID hits lines 83-85 and returns success without contacting the store, so `Authenticate` admits it. This bypasses the configured limit for the cache lifetime (29 minutes) and can be repeated whenever the entry expires. Only cache the ID after the database operation has succeeded, or remove the cache entry when it returns an error.

findings.title: The count-and-insert limit check is not atomic
findings.body: Each request independently counts active devices and then, if the count is below the limit, performs an upsert in a later database session. Concurrent requests for different new device IDs can all observe the same count below `deviceLimit` and all insert successfully, permanently exceeding the configured limit. Enforce the admission decision atomically, for example with a transaction and appropriate locking/serialization or a database-side conditional operation.

findings.title: An existing device can be rejected when MySQL reports a no-op update
findings.body: At capacity, existing devices are admitted by `updateDevice`, but it treats `RowsAffected() == 0` as proof that the device does not exist. MySQL normally reports zero affected rows when all assigned values are unchanged. In particular, Grafana already documents MySQL timestamp precision as seconds, so a request routed to another instance/restart in the same second with the same IP and user agent can assign the same stored `updated_at` value and be falsely returned as `ErrDeviceLimitReached`. This denies a device that should be allowed to refresh its existing record. Determine existence separately or use an update/result mode that distinguishes a matched row from a changed row.
